layers.name: Application Entry
layers.description: Spring Boot main class and constant definitions. DevorbitApiApplication bootstraps the entire service. CurriculumConstants defines SE2025 curriculum constants.

layers.name: Presentation / Controller Layer
layers.description: REST API controllers organized by access level: Admin (9), Public (6), Student (2), and PhotoboothFrame (1). Admin controllers manage courses, GitHub repos, repo candidates, roadmaps, notes, and auth. Public controllers expose courses, repos, AI queries, knowledge graph, discovery, and tech stacks. Student controllers handle auth and bookmarks.

layers.name: Service / Business Logic Layer
layers.description: Core business services implementing domain logic. Covers course management, GitHub repo scanning/approval, knowledge graph generation, learning roadmaps, photobooth, JWT auth, Supabase storage, student auth/bookmarks, and tech stack operations.

layers.name: AI / LLM Service Layer
layers.description: Specialized AI services for LLM-powered features: advice generation, curriculum matching, graph query engine (knowledge graph Q&A), roadmap generation, and content summarization.

layers.name: Repository / Data Access Layer
layers.description: Spring Data JPA repositories providing database access for all entities: courses, articles, relationships, tutorials, YouTube playlists, GitHub repos, repo candidates, learning roadmaps (items/phases), notes (code snippets), photobooth frames, bookmarks, admin users, student users, and tech stacks.

layers.name: Domain / Entity Layer
layers.description: JPA entity classes and enum types defining the domain model. Includes Course, GithubRepo, RepoCandidate, LearningRoadmap (with phases/items), Note (with code snippets), PhotoboothFrame, StudentUser/AdminUser, TechStack, CourseArticle/Tutorial/YoutubePlaylist, Bookmark, and Relationship. Enum types: CourseRelationType, NoteTargetType, RepoCandidateStatus, RoadmapItemTargetType.

layers.name: DTO / API Contract Layer
layers.description: Data Transfer Objects defining API request/response contracts. Organized by access level: admin (26 DTOs for login, courses, repos, candidates, roadmaps, notes, articles, tutorials, YouTube playlists), public (10 DTOs for AI queries, course details/summaries, elective groups, knowledge graph, repo summaries, roadmaps, tech stacks), and student (6 DTOs for auth, profile, bookmarks). Plus shared PhotoboothFrameDTO.

layers.name: Configuration & Security Layer
layers.description: Spring configuration classes, security setup, JWT auth filter/properties, GitHub client config/properties, Jackson config, OpenAPI/Swagger docs config, elective group config, and repo candidate data initializer (seeds data on startup).

layers.name: Exception & Event Handling
layers.description: Custom exception classes (BadRequestException, NotFoundException, UnauthorizedException) and a global ApiExceptionHandler for consistent error responses. Domain event (RelationshipChangedEvent) for course relationship changes.

layers.name: Database Schema & Migrations
layers.description: SQL schema definitions, seed data, Flyway migrations, and update scripts. schema.sql and schema-complete.sql define the full database schema. Flyway migration V002 adds photobooth frames. data.sql seeds initial courses, repos, tech stacks. Various update scripts for SE2025 curriculum and elective groups.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Deployment
layers.description: Deployment and runtime infrastructure. Dockerfile builds a multi-stage image (Maven + Temurin 21). Shell scripts (mvnw, run.bat) for building and running. backup_supabase.py for DB backups.

layers.name: Documentation & Agent Guides
layers.description: Project documentation files including architecture guide (ARCHITECTURE.md), agent operating guide (AGENTS.md), and per-layer AGENTS.md files for config, controller, entity, and service packages.

layers.name: Test Suite
layers.description: Integration and unit tests for controllers, services, and application context loading. Tests cover AdminCourse, AdminRepoCandidate, PublicCourse, PublicRepo controllers, and RepoCandidateService. Application context load test. Test config uses H2 in-memory database.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: Start at DevorbitApiApplication.java — the Spring Boot main class that bootstraps the entire service. This is where @SpringBootApplication scanning begins. Also review AGENTS.md for the project-level operating guide and ARCHITECTURE.md for the 3-layer architecture (Controller → Service → Repository) with request lifecycle tracing.

tour.title: Configuration & Security Setup
tour.description: Examine how DevOrbit is configured. pom.xml declares Spring Boot 4.0.6 with JPA, Security, JWT (jjwt 0.12.6), WebFlux, Flyway, and Lombok. application.yaml sets up database, JWT secrets, GitHub token, Supabase storage, CORS, and mail. SecurityConfig configures HTTP security. JwtAuthenticationFilter intercepts requests for /api/admin/** and /api/student/**. GitHub client, Jackson, OpenAPI/Swagger, and elective group configs are also wired here. .env.example shows the required runtime secrets.

tour.title: Domain Model — JPA Entities & Enums
tour.description: Explore the domain entities that model DevOrbit's core concepts: Course (with articles, tutorials, YouTube playlists, relationships), GithubRepo (scanned repos), RepoCandidate (pending approval workflow with status enum), LearningRoadmap (with phases and items), Note (with code snippets for any target type), PhotoboothFrame, StudentUser/AdminUser, and TechStack. Enum types like CourseRelationType, RepoCandidateStatus, NoteTargetType, and RoadmapItemTargetType define constrained values. Each entity maps to a PostgreSQL table via JPA annotations.

tour.title: Data Access — Spring Data JPA Repositories
tour.description: Learn how data flows to and from the database. Each entity has a corresponding Spring Data JPA repository interface (e.g., CourseRepository, GithubRepoRepository, RepoCandidateRepository). These provide CRUD, pagination, and custom query methods without boilerplate. PhotoboothFrameRepository and NoteRepository with NoteCodeSnippetRepository show more complex query patterns. StudentBookmarkRepository handles user-scoped data.

tour.title: Business Logic — Core Services
tour.description: Understand the service layer that implements domain logic. CourseService manages curriculum CRUD. GithubScanService orchestrates GitHub API scanning via WebClient. RepoCandidateService handles the candidate approval workflow. JwtService creates/validates JWT tokens. KnowledgeGraphService builds cross-course relationship graphs. AiService coordinates AI operations. SupabaseStorageService handles photobooth image uploads. LearningRoadmapService generates structured study plans.

tour.title: AI & LLM Service Integration
tour.description: Dive into the AI-powered features. GraphQueryEngine answers natural-language questions about the knowledge graph via LLM reasoning. RoadmapGenerator creates personalized learning roadmaps. CurriculumMatcher aligns courses to curriculum standards. AdviceGenerator provides course selection guidance. SummaryGenerator creates concise course descriptions. These services use WebClient to call an external LLM API and work alongside AiService for orchestration.

tour.title: REST API — Controllers by Access Level
tour.description: Trace how HTTP requests enter the system. Controllers are organized by access level. Admin controllers (AdminCourseController, AdminGithubController, AdminRepoCandidateController, AdminRoadmapController, AdminNoteController) handle CRUD behind JWT auth for /api/admin/**. Public controllers (PublicCourseController, PublicAiController, PublicDiscoveryController, PublicRepoController, PublicTechStackController) serve /api/public/** endpoints — course listings, AI queries, knowledge graph exploration, tech stacks. Student controllers (StudentAuthController, StudentBookmarkController) handle student auth and personalized bookmarks. PhotoboothFrameController manages photo frames.

tour.title: API Contracts — DTO Layer
tour.description: Understand how data is shaped for the wire. DTOs are organized by access: admin DTOs (LoginRequest/Response, CourseUpsertRequest, RepoCandidateResponse, RoadmapRequest/Response, ArticleRequest/Response, etc.), public DTOs (AiQueryRequest/Response, CourseDetailResponse, KnowledgeGraphResponse, TechStackResponse, etc.), and student DTOs (StudentLoginRequest, StudentRegisterRequest, StudentBookmarkRequest/Response, StudentProfileResponse). These prevent entity leaking and allow independent API evolution.

tour.title: Exception Handling & Domain Events
tour.description: See how errors are handled consistently. ApiExceptionHandler is a @RestControllerAdvice that catches custom exceptions (BadRequestException, NotFoundException, UnauthorizedException) and returns structured error responses. RelationshipChangedEvent is a Spring ApplicationEvent fired when course relationships change — trace how events decouple side effects from request processing.

tour.title: Database Schema, Migrations & Testing
tour.description: Finish with the data layer foundations. schema.sql and schema-complete.sql define the full PostgreSQL schema (with indexes, enums, constraints). Flyway migration V002 adds photobooth frames versioned. data.sql seeds initial courses, repos, and tech stacks. For confidence, review the test suite — controller tests use @WebMvcTest with mocked services and H2 in-memory DB; service tests verify business logic. application-test.yaml configures the test database.
